correctness.rationale: The 24-vertex truncated-cube skeleton built from 8 corner triangles and 12 axis-connection edges has exactly 36 undirected graph edges. The ordinary matching complex consists of ALL pairwise vertex-disjoint edge subsets. An independently authored C++ reconstruction (not opaque source execution) generated every one of 1,019,739 nonempty matchings and the exact matching-size distribution (36,558,4876,26421,92016,206676,292872,249420,117600,26928,2304,32). Independently repeated the 36-stage pivot matching: 509,667 matched pairs and residual one 0-cell, 368 7-cells, 36 8-cells. Exhaustive topological sort of all 7,220,436 oriented Hasse covers visited all 1,019,739 faces. Independently computed the exact signed integral Morse 368-by-36 boundary with 698 nonzero ±1 entries; elementary Z row/column steps obtained 36 unit pivots, all intermediate absolute entries ≤2. Hence its image is primitive rank 36, and since the 7-skeleton is 6-connected, Hurewicz turns the attaching maps into their integer degree vectors; 36 unit pairs cancel, giving ∨^332 S7 with no torsion. Logs alone, Euler characteristic alone and mod-two ranks would not prove this homotopy statement.

value.rationale: The truncated cube is a canonical Archimedean solid and cube-connected-cycles graph, making its ordinary matching complex a natural finite topological invariant. Its million-face structure reduces to a clean 332-sphere integral wedge only after a substantial full Morse and unimodularity calculation, a meaningful exact classification rather than a known-table recomputation. The result is useful as a benchmark for matching-complex topology on symmetric cubic graphs.
